findings.evidence: Check `command -v web2md`. If missing, point the user to the Installation section
findings.fix: The model already checks PATH and follows an install doc; keep only the non-obvious rule (do not invent a path or repository; there is no stderr until the binary runs) and move the generic check into README.md, recording the move.

findings.evidence: Procedure steps 2, 4 and 5 are each one dense paragraph covering destination choice, quoting, collisions, failure classes and the single retry.
findings.fix: Split each decision into a short branch the agent can follow: destination (print, one file, directory), quoting, collision, then failure class (timeout, thin body, login/consent) mapped to retry or stop. That is the Tool pattern this CLI task needs.

findings.evidence: Browser safety and gotchas cover sandbox, profile, interactive and untrusted page text, but not the CLI facts that defeat a reasonable retry: Readability can fall back to the whole body, and --wait-for is capped at the lower of --timeout-ms and 30s.
findings.fix: Add those two gotchas with why: a body-fallback page can look non-empty yet fail the heading-plus-several-sentences rule, and raising --timeout-ms does not extend a selector wait past 30s, so report that cap instead of retrying.

findings.evidence: Use only when the user explicitly says 'use the skill web-to-markdown' or 'use a skill web-to-markdown'; never for implicit requests.
findings.fix: Convert http(s) webpage URLs to clean Markdown with the locally installed web2md CLI (Puppeteer, Chromium, Readability, Turndown), including JS-rendered pages, login or consent walls, and batches. Use when the user asks to save, archive or print a page as Markdown, even if they do not name web2md, and also when they say 'use the skill web-to-markdown' or 'use a skill web-to-markdown'. Not for local HTML, PDFs, summaries, or general browser automation.

findings.evidence: See `web2md --help` for supported options. The body still inlines every flag recipe, quoting rule and failure class in steps 4 and 5.
findings.fix: Keep the decision tree in SKILL.md and move the quoting example, collision rule and retry recipe to references/web2md-options.md, with a step-4 trigger: read it when a URL contains a quote, several URLs share one path, or the first extraction fails. Do not load it for a single clean URL printed to stdout.

findings.evidence: an http(s) URL can contain a single quote or shell metacharacters, so pass one quoted argument per URL, wrap the URL in single quotes and write each ' inside it as '\''
findings.fix: Fragile shell quoting should be one exact argv form, not a recipe the agent rebuilds. State the default as a single argv array (no shell), and give one escape hatch: if the harness requires a shell, use the worked example `web2md 'https://example.com/o'\''brien' --print`.

findings.evidence: 11 evals assert behaviors in prose ('Recognizes explicit invocation', 'Retries once with --wait-until domcontentloaded') with no input files and no mechanically checkable expected command or output file.
findings.fix: Add evals/files/ fixtures for a thin body, a login wall and a navigation timeout, and assert the exact argv and the pass/fail classification against those fixtures.

findings.evidence: 10 should-trigger queries all contain the phrase 'use the skill web-to-markdown' or 'use a skill web-to-markdown'; none describes the task without naming the skill.
findings.fix: Replace half of the positives with realistic prompts that ask to archive or print a JS-rendered page as Markdown without naming the skill, and keep the near-miss negatives (WebFetch, local HTML, PDF, summary).

findings.evidence: Step 4 says 'Reject a URL only when it contains a newline or a null byte' after telling the agent to wrap the URL in single quotes, so a URL that is already rejected can still be interpolated.
findings.fix: Put the newline and null-byte check first and stop; only then quote. Add the missing branch: a non-zero exit that is not Chrome-not-found and not a navigation timeout (for example an HTTP error page that still returns a body) is reported with stderr and not retried.

The README example launches --interactive with no terminal check, which contradicts SKILL.md. Prefix it with the same gate: only when an attached human-controlled terminal exists; otherwise authenticate the dedicated profile externally and retry with --print.
